title: EEG during Balinese dance movements and balance tasks in expert dancers and non-dancers
description: Raw 16-channel EEG from 38 women (23 expert Balinese dancers and 15 non-dancers) recorded in a single session with two paradigms: three Balinese dance movements (ngeed, agem right, agem left) and a Romberg-type standing task. The dataset includes a separate resting recording, manually annotated movement-phase events, and Standing Stork balance times in the participants file. It supports research on cortical activity, motor expertise and postural balance in traditional dancers.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a KT88-1016 digital EEG system (Contec Medical Systems) using 16 dry scalp electrodes in a 10-20 layout without midline sites. Each electrode was referenced to the ipsilateral earlobe. Sampling rate was 100 Hz with an effective bandwidth of about 0.5-35 Hz. Movement phases (descent, hold, ascent) were annotated manually from video. Standing Stork times were measured with a Takei balance tester before the EEG session.
